deep.reconstruction:
This is a title page with no mathematics on it. The German text reads: 'Neue Beiträge zu den mathematischen Tafeln, besonders zur Erleichterung der Zalenrechnungen. Merz. 1795.' In English: 'New contributions to the mathematical tables, especially for easing numerical calculations. March 1795.' Around it are archival marks: the shelfmark 'Math. 2', an older number (40114) that has been struck through, a circled foliation '(1)', and the stamp of the Niedersächsische Staats- und Universitätsbibliothek Göttingen.

Context: In March 1795 Gauss was 17 and still at the Collegium Carolinum in Braunschweig. This was a few months before he went to Göttingen in October 1795, and about a year before the 17-gon discovery of March 1796. The title closely echoes J. H. Lambert's 'Zusätze zu den logarithmischen und trigonometrischen Tabellen zur Erleichterung und Abkürzung der bey Anwendung der Mathematik vorfallenden Berechnungen' (1770). Gauss is known to have used that work, with its factor and prime tables, at this period. That makes it plausible that the bundle collects his early table-making, such as factor tables, prime counts, and tables of decimal periods or residues. Nothing on this page can be reconstructed as a derivation.

results.what: Title of a planned or assembled collection of contributions to mathematical tables for easing numerical computation, dated March 1795
results.modern_name: Numerical tables / computational aids (cf. Lambert's 'Zusätze zu den Tabellen', 1770)
results.usually_credited_to: Tradition of Lambert, Vega and others; Gauss's early table work is documented in his Nachlass and Werke

deep.surprise_reason: This is a title page with no mathematical content. Gauss's early (1795) interest in computing and extending mathematical tables is well documented, and the title is modelled on Lambert's known work.
transcription_corrections: 'Zalenrechnungen' matches the manuscript's own archaic spelling (= Zahlenrechnungen) and should be kept as written.
'Merz.' is the manuscript's archaic spelling of 'März' (March); the date is March 1795.
The upper-right number '40114' is struck through in the image, as the [-...-] notation indicates; its exact digits are somewhat uncertain (possibly '40114' or '40/14').
